name: #BlackTechFutures Research Institute
description: Builds national network of HBCUs, city-based researchers, and community institutions focused on local Black tech ecosystems and tech talent. Received PIT Fund support to bolster Black civic tech workforce pipeline.
funding_detail: Public Interest Tech Fund ($250K grant) + philanthropic

name: Abundance New York
description: NYC-focused abundance advocacy organization pushing for housing supply expansion, zoning reform, and permitting streamlining at the city and state level.
funding_detail: Individual donors + paid subscribers; affiliated 501(c)(4) and 501(c)(3) entities

name: Alliance of Civic Technologists (ACT)
description: National umbrella connecting 18+ volunteer civic tech groups. Organizes CityCamp unconferences and Civic Spark convenings. 500+ Discord members.

name: Civic Tech Field Guide
description: Largest open catalog of civic tech projects and organizations worldwide, with the Field Guide Friday newsletter (4,300+ subscribers). Serves as a discovery tool for technologists entering the field.

name: Demand Progress
description: Progressive advocacy organization with a congressional modernization portfolio covering transparency, open data, and legislative branch capacity. Co-authored bipartisan House rules reform proposals with Lincoln Network.

name: Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF)
description: Leading nonprofit defending civil liberties in the digital world through litigation, policy advocacy, and technology development. Shapes government surveillance law, AI policy, and digital rights frameworks.
funding_detail: Individual members; Ford Foundation, MacArthur Foundation, Open Society Foundations

name: Federation of American Scientists (FAS)
description: Nonpartisan think tank running Day One Project for policy entrepreneurship. Innovation Ecosystem Job Board for displaced federal technologists (2025). Senior Fellows program.
funding_detail: Schmidt Futures, Coefficient Giving (fmr. Open Philanthropy), broad base

name: Inclusive Abundance
description: Coalition of center-left and center-right organizations advancing the abundance agenda: housing supply, energy permitting, regulatory reform, and state capacity. Members include FAS, Niskanen Center, R Street, and New America.

name: Institute for Responsive Government (IRG)
description: Designs policy solutions for government service delivery and election administration, including automatic voter registration, cross-agency data sharing, and UX reform for DMVs, tax departments, and benefits offices. Research is aimed at state legislators and local administrators. Fiscally sponsored by New Venture Fund, with a separate 501(c)(4) arm (Responsive Gov Action).
funding_detail: New Venture Fund fiscal sponsorship; philanthropic grants

name: National Conference on Citizenship (NCoC) / Project Redesign
description: Civic health research. Project Redesign focuses on redesigning public services. Co-created TELI program.

name: New Practice Lab
description: New America initiative working to improve government program design for families through policy advocacy and implementation sprints with government agencies.

name: Open New York
description: NYC-based advocacy organization pushing for housing supply expansion through zoning reform and land use deregulation. Primary policy focus is increasing housing production in New York City.

name: Open The Government
description: Coalition advocating for government transparency, open data, and accountability. Works on FOIA reform, open data policy, and government information access. Part of broader good-government advocacy ecosystem.

name: Partnership for Public Service
description: Nonpartisan organization working for better government and a stronger civil service. Advocates for reform through its Government for a New Era initiative and trains public servants at the federal, state, and local levels.
funding_detail: Broad philanthropic base; earned revenue from training

name: POPVOX Foundation
description: Congressional modernization nonprofit focused on AI-ready legislatures and legislative branch capacity. Key 2025 wins: secured 4M House Modernization Initiatives Account; advanced CaseCompass unified casework data schema; launched Digital Parliaments Project globally. Runs Future-Proofing Congress newsletter, Casework Navigator, and Keeping Pace AI briefing for Congressional staff.
funding_detail: Hewlett Foundation, Democracy Fund, philanthropic grants

name: Public Interest Technology University Network (PIT-UN)
description: Network of 63 universities co-convened by New America, Ford Foundation, and Hewlett Foundation. $16M+ deployed to 154 projects building the PIT field through curriculum, faculty research, and experiential learning.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Hewlett Foundation, Mastercard, McGovern, Raikes, Schmidt Futures, Siegel

name: Recoding America Fund
description: $120M 6-year pooled philanthropic initiative grantmaking for government workforce, digital infrastructure, and procedural reform. Chaired by Jennifer Pahlka.
funding_detail: Pooled fund; early backers include Arnold Ventures, Alta Futures, and Packard Foundation

name: Results for America
description: Helps government use evidence and data. Runs What Works Cities and States certifications promoting performance management and evidence-based policymaking.

name: Tech Talent Project
description: Connects senior technologists with government roles and helps new administrations build tech leadership from day one, including first-100-days playbooks for states. Co-runs TELI executive training with Aspen Policy Academy. Has matched technical leaders with state and local governments since 2017.

name: Work for America
description: Advocacy organization working to modernize government hiring and talent pipelines, combining direct workforce programs with HR policy advocacy.

name: Apolitical
description: Global social learning network for public servants, with 500,000+ members in 170 countries, including 50,000+ US civil servants. Offers online courses on digital government and AI, including the Government AI Campus (launched 2023). Approved supplier on multiple government learning procurement frameworks.
funding_detail: Government contracts (UK, US, and other governments); subscription fees

name: Aspen Policy Academy (fmr. Aspen Tech Policy Hub)
description: S&T Policy Training (3-week intensive), TELI exec program (5-week, 150+ alumni), Primer, and short courses training STEM professionals on policy impact.
funding_detail: Craig Newmark Philanthropies, Ford Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment

name: Center for Civic Futures (CCF) / AI Readiness Project
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit running the AI Readiness Project and the State Chief AI Officer Community of Practice (30+ states). Houses the Public Benefit Innovation Fund, which awarded $8.5M to eight state AI benefits projects in Dec 2025. Runs structured pilots for responsible AI in public service.
funding_detail: Rockefeller Foundation ($500K+ for AI Readiness); PBIF partners Ballmer Group, Gates Foundation, W.K. Kellogg Foundation, Renaissance Philanthropy, Families and Workers Fund

name: Civic Tech Institute (Equitech Futures)
description: 10-week fully funded cohort program training early-career professionals in data science, AI, and civic innovation. Certificate + 1-year alumni mentorship.

name: Decoded Futures (Tech:NYC Foundation)
description: AI capacity-building for NYC nonprofits delivering public services. Cohort-based AI training, industry tech mentors, prototyping support, and grants ($5K-$100K/org).
funding_detail: Robin Hood, Google.org, Salesforce, OpenAI, Altman Foundation, AWS

name: InnovateUS
description: Free digital and AI skills training for public servants, with 200,000+ learners across 50 states and 80 countries and 100+ agency partners. A $5M Google.org grant (2025) funds expansion to 100,000+ more state and local workers. Founded by Beth Simone Noveck at Northeastern University's Burnes Center.
funding_detail: Google.org (5M grant 2025); Hewlett Foundation; philanthropic grants

name: National Academy of Public Administration (NAPA)
description: Congressionally chartered. Convenes expert panels studying federal agency management, organizational design, and institutional effectiveness.

name: Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP): AI Expo / Talent Initiatives
description: Eric Schmidt-founded initiative (2022) on U.S. technological competitiveness in AI and advanced technology. Produces policy recommendations, convenes government and industry leaders, and hosts the annual AI Expo for National Competitiveness in DC, shaping AI talent and government technology workforce policy.

name: BetaNYC
description: NYC civic tech, open data, and open government nonprofit (est. 2013). Co-produces NYC Open Data Week with OTI (6,000+ participants in 2026, its tenth year), hosts the NYC School of Data conference, and runs Civic Innovation Fellows. ACT founding member.
funding_detail: Small grants; NYC OTI partnership; volunteer-driven

name: Chi Hack Night
description: Chicago civic tech meetup (est. 2012; 690+ events) meeting monthly in person and three times a month online, with speakers from government, nonprofits, and tech. Spawned projects including mRelief. Elected board; ACT founding member.

name: Civic Tech Atlanta
description: Atlanta civic tech group (fmr. Code for Atlanta) that hosted hack nights at Tech Square ATL and provided data support to community organizations. Last documented activity (2024). ACT founding member.

name: Civic Tech DC
description: Washington DC volunteer civic tech group (est. 2012) meeting about twice a month to build tools with community organizations and government agencies. Hosted Civic Hack DC 2025 on Regulations.gov public comment analysis. ACT member.

name: Code for Boston
description: Boston-area civic tech group running hybrid hack nights at Cambridge Innovation Center. Builds MAPLE (Massachusetts Platform for Legislative Engagement) for submitting legislative testimony. ACT founding member.

name: Code for BTV
description: Burlington, VT civic tech group working as a pro bono digital agency for civic and social justice organizations, with biweekly virtual Action Nights. ACT founding member.

name: Code for Charlottesville
description: Charlottesville, VA civic tech group doing pro bono projects with local nonprofits and government agencies, with UVA and PVCC student involvement. GitHub activity through 2025 includes a Virginia schools AI policy analysis. ACT member.

name: Code for Dayton
description: Dayton civic tech group with monthly meetings. Projects include Florence Nightingale Museum website and demolition permit monitoring for Preservation Dayton. ACT founding member.

name: Code for Philly
description: Philadelphia civic tech community. Projects include Clean & Green Philly (vacant lot greening to reduce gun violence), Phlask (map of free water, food, and bathrooms), and a Benefit Decision Toolkit. ACT founding member.

name: Code with the Carolinas
description: Carolinas civic tech community, independent of the Code for America Brigade Network since 2023 and fiscally sponsored through Open Collective. Joined ACT in spring 2025; projects include Open Sidewalks accessibility mapping and Zoning Atlas.

name: ELGL (Engaging Local Government Leaders)
description: 501(c)(3) network of 4,800+ local government leaders across all 50 states. Runs the GovLove podcast, Top Influencers awards, Analyst Academy, and Public Service Recognition Week.

name: Florida Community Innovation (FCI)
description: Florida civic tech organization running the Florida Resource Map project and an AI Fellow program. Published an organizational handbook (2025). ACT member.

name: GovLoop
description: Online community of 300,000+ government professionals. Featured Contributor Program, NextGen Government Training Summit, and educational resources on modernization, AI, and workforce. Knowledge-sharing platform connecting public servants across levels.
funding_detail: GovExec Media / Owned by Government Executive Media Group; sponsor-supported content

name: Hack for LA
description: Los Angeles network of civic-minded technologists building digital products with community partners and local government. Global volunteer base (designers, developers, PMs). Maintains Civic Tech Index.

name: Open Austin
description: Central Texas civic tech nonprofit (est. 2009; 501(c)(3) since 2018) that has trained 1,500+ members. Its Civic Digital Lab builds data and web tools for local agencies and advocacy groups, and it runs a Civic Data Fellowship. ACT and Electronic Frontier Alliance member.

name: Open Sacramento
description: Sacramento civic tech group (recently rebranded with new website). Virtual community action nights. ACT member.

name: Open Source San Jose
description: San Jose civic tech collective running monthly hack nights (ACT member since 2025). Building Tally Up, a meal distribution tracking app for the CA Department of Education.

name: OpenOakland
description: Oakland civic tech group building tools for government transparency and community access. ACT member.

name: SF Civic Tech
description: San Francisco civic tech community (fmr. Code for San Francisco, est. 2013), independent 501(c)(3) since 2024. Runs weekly virtual hack nights and is building the SafeHome earthquake risk dashboard. ACT founding member.

name: Technologists for the Public Good (TPG)
description: 501(c)(6) professional association (est. 2020) for public interest technologists across government, nonprofits, academia, and civic tech. Runs networking events, conferences, mentorship, and the Tech to Gov Virtual Forum & Job Fair. Co-hosted State of GovTech 2025 with CivStart.

name: Civic Analytics Network (GovEx)
description: Peer network of city chief data officers and senior data officials (est. 2015 by Harvard's Ash Center with UChicago), now convened by the Bloomberg Center for Government Excellence at Johns Hopkins. Members share innovations in public sector data, analytics, and AI.
funding_detail: Founded with an Arnold Foundation grant; now convened by GovEx (Johns Hopkins)

name: Ad Hoc
description: Federal digital services firm founded in 2014 out of the healthcare.gov rescue. Work includes VA.gov (consolidating 500+ sites), Medicare Plan Finder, and Search.gov. Builds agency capacity through embedded product teams.

name: Agile Six
description: Public benefit corporation delivering human-centered digital services to federal agencies. Primary focus on VA digital services and benefits delivery, CDC pandemic readiness, and CMS Medicare modernization. Fully remote, values-driven culture.

name: Behavioural Insights Team (BIT)
description: Behavioral science consultancy founded inside the UK government in 2010, now owned by Nesta, with US offices in New York and DC. Designs and tests government programs with RCTs, including 95+ with US cities through What Works Cities.
funding_detail: Government contracts and philanthropy (Bloomberg Philanthropies, What Works Cities); owned by Nesta charity

name: Bloom Works
description: Digital services consultancy delivering user research, service design, engineering, and content strategy to government agencies. Focus on healthcare.gov and social services modernization. Woman-owned small business.

name: Civic Consulting Alliance
description: Chicago-based nonprofit (est. 1985) providing $15-30M/year in pro bono consulting to city and county government. Mobilizes corporate partners (BCG, Deloitte, McKinsey, etc.) for systems-level projects on economic development, education, safety, and health. $200M+ total investment facilitated.
funding_detail: MacArthur Foundation, corporate pro bono partners, philanthropic grants

name: Civic Design Collaborative
description: Human-centered design and civic innovation consultancy working with government agencies on service delivery improvement.

name: CivicActions
description: Twenty years delivering digital services to federal and state agencies - open-source by default and outcomes-focused. Current portfolio includes healthcare.gov, medicare.gov, cms.gov, nsf.gov, and va.gov, with deep practice in agile delivery, user-centered design, accessibility compliance, DevSecOps, and responsible AI-enabled modernization.

name: Civilla
description: Nonprofit design studio changing how public-serving institutions work through human-centered redesign of forms, processes, and services. Redesigned Michigan's public benefits application (Harvard Innovations in Government recognition). Partners with the Beeck Center.
funding_detail: Philanthropic grants + earned revenue from government partnerships

name: Code for America
description: Civic tech nonprofit (est. 2009) building digital tools and changing policies across the safety net, criminal justice, and tax systems. Its $100M Safety Net Innovation Lab has partnered with 14 states, DC, and the Cherokee Nation. Hosts the annual Code for America Summit.

name: Coforma
description: Federal digital services firm with strong portfolio in healthcare and civic technology (healthcare.gov, VA, USDS partnerships). SBA-certified.

name: Greater Good Studio
description: Chicago-based design studio applying human-centered design to complex social challenges, including government service delivery, health equity, and criminal justice. Maintains a database of social impact-oriented design professionals and organizations available at greatergoodstudio.com/database. Works with government agencies, nonprofits, and foundations.

name: GreenInfo Network
description: Nonprofit providing GIS, mapping, and data services primarily to government agencies and advocacy organizations. Notable California state agency relationships.

name: Harvard Government Performance Lab (GPL)
description: Harvard Kennedy School lab embedding full-time fellows in state and local agencies for 12-36 month pro bono reform projects in child welfare, criminal justice, homelessness, housing, and procurement. Has worked with 112 jurisdictions in 38 states on 278+ projects shifting $7B+ in spending.
funding_detail: Bloomberg Philanthropies, Rockefeller Foundation + Harvard Kennedy School

name: Illinois Digital Service
description: Nonprofit (fiscally sponsored by Digital Harbor Foundation) providing pro bono digital services to Illinois state and local agencies. Small team with federal and state government backgrounds, working embedded with agency staff across product, UX research, service design, engineering, and data.
funding_detail: Families and Workers Fund, P33, Origami Works Foundation; fiscally sponsored by Digital Harbor Foundation

name: Mighty Acorn Digital
description: Digital services firm providing product management and delivery support to government agencies.

name: mRelief
description: Nonprofit building text and web screeners that help residents check eligibility for SNAP, Medicaid, and other benefits. Grew out of Chi Hack Night; partners with city governments and social service organizations.

name: Nava PBC
description: Public benefit corporation delivering agile software development, user-centered design, and cloud engineering to government agencies. Built Healthcare.gov fixes and VA.gov. ~200 employees focused exclusively on government digital services.

name: Partners for Public Good (PPG)
description: Independent nonprofit spun out of Harvard GPL's procurement initiative in March 2025. Helps state and local governments improve procurement, staffing, digital infrastructure, and budgeting, with 200+ jurisdictions served. Runs the Procurement Excellence Network (2,000+ officials across 50 states).

name: Public Policy Lab
description: Nonprofit innovation lab applying human-centered design to government service delivery through direct government agency contracts and grants.

name: Skylight Digital
description: Digital government consultancy delivering agile procurement support, user-centered design, cloud and DevOps, and API-first architecture to federal and state agencies. Won a $14M CMS task order (2026) to help states implement Medicaid community engagement requirements. HUBZone-certified small business.

name: Third Sector Capital Partners
description: Nonprofit TA firm helping government agencies design and implement outcomes-focused contracting, Pay for Success structures, and data-driven service delivery. Government agencies are primary clients.

name: Truss
description: Federal digital services firm with strong portfolio including IRS Direct File, USWDS contributions, .gov registrar, and VA work. 8(a) SBA certified.

name: U.S. Digital Response (USDR)
description: Matches 11,000+ volunteer technologists with governments for pro bono help on digital services, procurement, talent, AI, and language access; 600+ engagements across federal, state, local, and tribal governments. Publishes practical toolkits, including a 2026 guide to launching digital service teams, and runs the Digital Service Champions Awards.

name: VotingWorks
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit building open-source, publicly owned voting machines and election auditing software. Only nonprofit building certified voting systems in the US. Deployed in multiple states.
funding_detail: Philanthropic grants; nonprofit; only certified nonprofit voting system builder in US

name: Abundance Network
description: National network connecting organizations and advocates advancing abundance-oriented policy reform across housing, energy, and permitting. Functions as a coordinating infrastructure for the broader abundance movement.

name: Accelerator for America
description: Mayor-led nonprofit co-founded by Eric Garcetti giving cities technical assistance on federal funding, infrastructure, and economic development. Active in 60+ cities, supporting smart city plans, EDA Tech Hubs applications, and ballot initiatives.

name: All Tech Is Human
description: Responsible tech ecosystems org. Slack community, job board, and mentorship program connecting people to careers in public interest technology. Focuses on diversifying the pipeline into tech policy and civic tech roles.

name: ASTHO (Association of State and Territorial Health Officials)
description: Association of state and territorial public health officials (59 jurisdictions). A CDC-designated national partner for the Public Health Infrastructure Grant (PHIG), supporting 107 health departments; CDC cut PHIG awards to four states in Feb 2026, now in litigation. Co-launched the $255M Public Health Data Modernization Implementation Center Program (2024).
funding_detail: CDC cooperative agreements (primary, including $155M+ PHIG share) + membership dues from state/territorial health officials + federal grants

name: Bloomberg Cities Network
description: JHU-hosted peer network for city leaders and innovators, created in partnership with Bloomberg Philanthropies. Provides peer networking, idea exchange, training resources, and city solution replication infrastructure. Distinct from the Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative (training) and Bloomberg Philanthropies Government Innovation (grantmaking).

name: Bloomberg Philanthropies City Data Alliance
description: Bloomberg Philanthropies program investing 60 million to help cities across the Americas build data infrastructure and AI readiness. 65 cities across 12 countries in current cohort. Structured peer learning model: mayors and chief data officers receive training, tools, and peer network access to advance data-driven governance.

name: City Innovate
description: San Francisco-based nonprofit running the Startup in Residence (STIR) program, connecting startups to government agencies to co-design technology solutions for defined government challenges. Structured procurement reform model that creates a path from co-design to contract. Operates nationally.

name: CivStart
description: Nonprofit govtech accelerator for state and local government, with six cohorts and 71+ startups scaled. Runs a 12-month accelerator, GovTech Lab, and a Venture Partner Network; its recent cohort focused on AI in local government with NLC and GovAI Coalition.
funding_detail: Foundation grants; government and corporate partnerships

name: Colorado Smart Cities Alliance
description: Statewide coalition of government, business, and academic partners convening around smart city technology adoption in Colorado. Runs challenge-based procurement programs, pilots, and the Smart Futures Lab accelerator. Member of the National Smart Coalitions Partnership.

name: GovAI Coalition
description: Coalition of 3,000+ public servants from 900+ agencies promoting responsible public sector AI. Founded by the City of San Jose in 2023; became an independent nonprofit in 2026. Produces AI policy templates, vendor AI FactSheets, use case libraries, and an AI Contract Hub.
funding_detail: City of San Jose (founding host); Packard Foundation ($150K nonprofit transition grant, 2026); member contributions

name: HSITAG (Human Services IT Advisory Group)
description: Nonprofit trade association under CompTIA (founded 1993, 123 member companies) bridging health and human services IT vendors and government HHS agencies. Advises federal and state HHS technology procurement officials.
funding_detail: Member dues from 123 technology companies; CompTIA affiliation

name: Illinois Smart City and Region Association (ISCRA)
description: 501c3 nonprofit association bringing municipalities and technology vendors together in a neutral forum to advance smart city and region initiatives across Illinois. Member of the National Smart Coalitions Partnership.

name: KC Digital Drive
description: Kansas City-based nonprofit founded in 2012 to make the region a digital leader. Runs Code for KC, convenes the KC Coalition for Digital Inclusion, and hosts civic tech and smart city programs. Member of the National Smart Coalitions Partnership.

name: Leading Cities
description: Global city network running AcceliGOV, which deploys vetted smart city solutions into municipalities through 90-day paid pilots and handles sourcing, vetting, and deployment. 32+ projects completed, targeting 100 resilience projects by 2030 across flood risk, water, mobility, and infrastructure.
funding_detail: Philanthropic grants + corporate partnerships + city engagement fees

name: NASCIO (National Association of State Chief Information Officers)
description: Peer network, research body, and voice for state CIOs. Runs the annual State CIO Survey and State CIO Top 10 Priorities, plus research with McKinsey, EY, and Deloitte on GenAI, cybersecurity, and data. Hosts national conferences and the State IT Recognition Awards.
funding_detail: State membership dues + corporate associate program + conference revenue

name: National Association of State Workforce Agencies (NASWA)
description: Association (est. 1937) of state workforce agencies in all 50 states, DC, and territories. Runs shared UI and workforce technology infrastructure, including the IT Support Centers, UI SIDES, and the National Labor Exchange. Partnered with the Beeck Center and DOL on the Open UI Initiative.
funding_detail: Membership dues from 50 state workforce agencies + federal contracts and cooperative agreements (DOL); CESER 501(c)(3) arm receives federal grants

name: NNPHI (National Network of Public Health Institutes)
description: Association of 40+ state and regional public health institutes. A CDC-designated national partner for the Public Health Infrastructure Grant (PHIG), providing TA through nine Regional Innovation Hubs; CDC cut PHIG awards to four states in Feb 2026, now in litigation. Co-launched the $255M Public Health Data Modernization Implementation Center Program (2024).
funding_detail: CDC cooperative agreements (primary, including PHIG share) + member fees + federal and foundation grants (Robert Wood Johnson Foundation, HHS Office of Minority Health)

name: North Texas Innovation Alliance (NTXIA)
description: 501c3 regional consortium of 50+ municipalities, agencies, corporations, and academic institutions across North Texas. Facilitates call-for-innovation programs, procurement reform, and smart region strategy. Largest initiative of its kind in the US.

name: Partnership Fund for NYC
description: NYC-based evergreen fund running structured challenge programs connecting early-stage startups to public agencies (MTA, Port Authority, NYCHA) for proof-of-concept pilots and procurement pathways. Has brokered 32 million+ in government contracts. Ecosystem intermediary bridging GovTech vendors and city government.

name: SETDA (State Educational Technology Directors Association)
description: National association (founded 2001) of state and territorial education technology leaders, including state education agency CIOs. Publishes the annual State EdTech Trends report and procurement guidance, and builds state education agency capacity to adopt technology responsibly.
funding_detail: State education agency membership dues + foundation grants (Siegel Family Endowment, Google.org) + federal education grants

name: Smart North Florida (SNF)
description: Nonprofit dedicated to harnessing regional collaboration, data coordination, and smart technologies to improve Northeast Florida economic competitiveness, sustainability, and quality of life. Member of the National Smart Coalitions Partnership.

name: Southern Arizona Smart Region (Regional Partnering Center)
description: Greater Tucson regional smart city initiative led by the Regional Partnering Center, a public-private partnership. Works to build economic competitiveness and quality of life through collaborative smart region strategy. Member of the National Smart Coalitions Partnership.

name: The Connective
description: Greater Phoenix smart region consortium launched in 2019. Partners public sector, academia, industry, and civic institutions to co-design and deploy technology solutions for regional challenges. Problem-driven model: cities surface needs, the Connective facilitates solution development.

name: US Ignite
description: National nonprofit (NSF-originated) providing technical assistance and capacity-building to communities navigating broadband deployment and smart city development. Manages federal funding identification tools, runs community programs including Project OVERCOME, and operates the PAWR advanced wireless research platform.
funding_detail: NSF, Schmidt Futures, Knight Foundation; federal program funding

name: AAAS S&T Policy Fellowships
description: 1-2 year fellowships placing scientists and engineers in federal agencies and Congress. Expanded AI tracks. 3,500+ alumni since 1973.

name: California Capital Fellows Program
description: Four fellowships (Assembly, Senate, Executive, Judicial) placing 64 fellows/year at highest levels of CA state government for 10-11 months. Fellows assist legislators, senior executive staff, and court administrators on policy. Nationally recognized.

name: CCST (California Council on Science and Technology)
description: Hybrid research and fellowship organization placing 10-15 PhD-level fellows annually into the California Legislature and Executive Branch. One of the longest-running state-level science fellowship programs in the US.

name: CivicSpark (AmeriCorps)
description: 11-month AmeriCorps fellowship placing ~150 fellows/year in local governments and community orgs for capacity building on climate, housing, water, transportation, public health. 1,000+ alumni since 2014. Expanding beyond CA/CO/WA to all states starting 2025.
funding_detail: AmeriCorps federal funding + local agency cost-share ($37,500/fellow)

name: Coding it Forward Fellowship
description: 10-week paid summer placement of early-career technologists in federal, state, and local government. Five tracks: data, design, product, software, cybersecurity. 700+ alumni.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment, McGovern Foundation, Pivotal Ventures

name: Cornell Tech PiTech Initiative
description: PhD Impact Fellowships, Visiting Practitioner's Program, and PiTech Impact Studio for graduate students working on public interest technology.

name: Coro Fellows Program in Public Affairs
description: 7-9 month full-time leadership fellowship rotating fellows through government, nonprofit, business, and labor placements. 80+ year track record and 15,000+ alumni; programs in LA, SF, NYC, Pittsburgh, and St. Louis.

name: DC Capital City Fellows Program (CCFP)
description: 18-month mayoral initiative placing recent masters graduates in DC government agencies. Three 6-month rotations across government operations, health/human services, public safety, planning, or education. Entry salary ~$62K.

name: FUSE Corps
description: Executive fellowship embedding experienced private-sector leaders in city and county agencies for one- or two-year strategic projects. Has led 400+ projects in 58 governments across 26 states; its fall 2026 cohort serves about 20 governments.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Hewlett Foundation, Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Irvine Foundation

name: Georgetown McCourt Tech & Policy Visiting Fellows
description: Semester-long visiting fellowship for tech policy practitioners at Georgetown McCourt School. Multiple USDS alumni and former federal tech officials in inaugural 2025 cohort. Fellows write policy essays, mentor students, and conduct research.

name: Govern for America (GFA)
description: Two-year paid fellowship placing recent graduates in high-impact state/local government roles. Published AI x Talent research for states.

name: Harvard Ash Center Democracy Fellowships
description: Financial support for doctoral and postdoctoral researchers studying democratic governance, innovation in government, and civic technology. Part of the Ash Center's Program on Democratic Governance.

name: Horizon Institute for Public Service
description: Places experts in AI, biotechnology, and other emerging technologies in federal agencies, congressional offices, and think tanks for up to two years, after part-time policy training. Community of 100+ fellows and alumni.

name: Judicial Innovation Fellowship (Georgetown)
description: 1-year fellowship placing technologists, designers, and user testers in state, local, tribal, and territorial courts to build data infrastructure, simplify processes, and improve access to justice. Inaugural cohort 2023-24. Incubated at Georgetown Law's Institute for Technology Law & Policy.

name: Lead for America
description: AmeriCorps-backed fellowship placing young leaders in local governments and nonprofits in their hometowns, focused on rural and underserved communities. Runs the American Connection Corps digital inclusion program.

name: Media Democracy Fund Fellowships
description: Technology Exchange (12+ months at civil society orgs) and PhDX Fellowship (PhD students at DC policy orgs). Focused on public interest technology and media policy.

name: NobleReach Scholars (NobleReach Foundation)
description: 1-2 year fully paid fellowship placing early-career technologists (AI, cybersecurity, process innovation) in federal, state, and local government. Launched 2024; the 2025 cohort of 28 included state and local placements such as Oklahoma City, Pittsburgh, and Maryland DoIT. NobleReach is the founding nonprofit partner of OPM's U.S. Tech Force.
funding_detail: $400M+ endowment from LMI Consulting divestiture; fellows receive full salary + $15K stipend

name: Paragon Policy Fellowship
description: Remote, unpaid fellowship in which university students and recent graduates work in project teams on technology policy research for state and local government partners, 8-10 hours a week.

name: S&T Impact Advisory Group
description: Advisory and program support organization helping science and technology fellowship programs launch and scale. Works with state legislatures and agencies to develop new S&T fellowship capacity.

name: S&T Impact: State Legislative Futures Forum
description: Partnership with TechCongress to extend tech policy fellowship model to state legislatures. Inaugural State Legislative Futures Forum held in DC 2025. Trains technologists on state-level policymaking.

name: TechCongress
description: Bipartisan fellowship placing technologists as policy advisors in congressional offices and committees for up to a year. Its 16th cohort (2026, 15 fellows) expanded to digital service delivery, climate, criminal justice, and space; 30 of 123+ alumni converted to full-time Hill staff.
funding_detail: Hewlett Foundation, Omidyar Network, Ford Foundation

name: xD (U.S. Census Bureau)
description: Emerging technology fellowship for mid-career technologists at Census Bureau focused on AI/ML, data engineering, and emerging tech.

name: 18F (GSA)
description: Defunct (Mar 2025). Former GSA consultancy that provided agile development, procurement consulting, user research, and open-source tooling to federal agencies; alumni continue its open-source resources externally.

name: ACF Digital Service
description: Digital service team within the Administration for Children and Families (HHS). Builds and improves technology for federal child welfare, TANF, and human services programs. Verified active with 11-15 FTE.

name: Arizona Strategic Enterprise Technology Office (ADOA-ASET)
description: Statewide IT strategy and digital services division of the Arizona Department of Administration. Closed 90 on-premises data centers, migrated 2,900+ applications, and runs the Office of Digital Solutions managing 200+ agency websites and Business One Stop. Earned an A- on the 2024 Digital States Survey.
funding_detail: AZ state general fund; Web Portal Fund; ADOA automation operations fund

name: Arlington County Digital Innovation
description: County digital innovation division with 7+ year AI program. Operates virtual assistant 'Ava', enterprise data warehouse, and open-source ML tools.

name: ARPA-H
description: Funds high-risk, high-reward health research via ARPA model: empowered program managers, milestone-based funding, other transaction authority. ~$1.5B annual budget.

name: Austin Office of Design & Delivery
description: Municipal digital services team providing service design, user research, content strategy, and digital forms for city services.

name: Baltimore Digital
description: Digital services team within the Baltimore Mayor's Office. Focuses on human-centered design and resident-facing digital service delivery. Confirmed active under Mayor Brandon Scott administration.

name: BIA Indigenous Connectivity and Technology Division
description: Bureau of Indian Affairs division (est. 2022-2023) providing technical assistance to Tribal Nations on broadband, spectrum leasing, and digital capacity, coordinating with FCC, NTIA, and Commerce. Operational status since January 2025 is unconfirmed; its web content was archived at the change of administration.

name: Boston Department of Innovation and Technology (DoIT)
description: City of Boston's enterprise technology organization (~150 staff) serving 18,000+ city employees. The City Council codified DoIT in May 2025, giving it formal authority over citywide technology procurement, cybersecurity, and data governance. Manages BOS:311, digital services, Wicked Free Wi-Fi, and a Digital Equity Fund.
funding_detail: City of Boston budget; federal digital equity grants (MBI Partnership Grant)

name: California Office of Data & Innovation (ODI)
description: Statewide digital services and data team in the Government Operations Agency, delivering user research, content design, data analytics, and plain language guidance across CA state agencies. Houses the State Chief Data Officer and publishes the statewide data strategy (2026-27 edition).

name: Chicago Department of Technology and Innovation (DTI)
description: Citywide technology department created in late 2023 to consolidate and rethink Chicago's IT. Maintains the Chicago Design System and coordinates technology across city departments to reduce complexity and improve digital services.

name: City and County of Denver - Peak Academy & Technology Services
description: Two city capacity units. Peak Academy has trained 11,000+ Denver employees and staff from 350+ governments in lean process improvement since 2012, saving $75M+. Technology Services runs an Automation Center of Excellence that saved $2.9M and 54,000 staff hours (2024 Apex Project of the Year).
funding_detail: City and County of Denver general fund

name: CMS Digital Service (DSAC)
description: Digital services team within the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services. Responsible for healthcare.gov recovery, 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, and the first federal open source program office (OSPO). One of the most impactful federal digital service teams.

name: CODE PA
description: Commonwealth Office of Digital Experience, created by executive order in 2023; grew from 3 staff to about 50. Delivers human-centered design, accessibility, and digital service improvements across PA agencies, reporting to both the state CIO and the Governor's office.

name: Colorado Digital Service
description: State digital team within the Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT), founded by USDS alumni, using product management, user research, and agile delivery. In 2026 OIT adopted the CDS model statewide: its director became state CIO and OIT cut 173 management roles.

name: Connecticut Digital Government Team
description: State digital services team within Connecticut Department of Administrative Services. Operational since 2019 with 21-25 FTE.

name: Delaware Government Information Center
description: Delaware central digital services and government information team, operational since 2001. Manages state web properties, open data, and digital service delivery. Verified active with 11-15 FTE.

name: Federal Student Aid Digital Services
description: Digital service team within Federal Student Aid (FSA), established 2024 under FSA OCTO. Focused on modernizing federal student aid technology and improving applicant experience for 40 million+ borrowers.

name: Franklin County GX Foundry
description: Digital services and government experience team for Franklin County, Ohio (Columbus metro). Verified active with 16-20 FTE and 2 million budget.

name: Georgia Digital Services and Solutions
description: Digital services team within the Georgia Technology Authority (GTA) managing state web infrastructure, UX, and accessibility (GovHub platform). Distinct from the Georgia Office of Artificial Intelligence, also a GTA sub-program focused on AI governance.

name: Georgia Office of Artificial Intelligence
description: Dedicated state AI office within the Georgia Technology Authority. Published the state AI Roadmap and Governance Framework and drives a cloud-first initiative with AI integration, backed by $15M in additional cybersecurity and AI funding.

name: Gilbert, AZ Office of Digital Government
description: City digital government office delivering social media strategy, open data, civic engagement, and digital innovation. Nationally recognized.

name: Hennepin County Digital Experience (DX)
description: Digital services and experience team for Hennepin County, Minnesota (Minneapolis metro). Verified active with 21-25 FTE. One of the largest county-level digital service teams in the US.

name: House Digital Service (HDS)
description: Digital service team for the US House of Representatives, established 2019. Serves the legislative branch, distinct from executive branch digital service teams.

name: Illinois Department of Innovation & Technology (DoIT)
description: Illinois enterprise IT agency (est. 2018 by statute) serving 36 client agencies and 90+ government entities, including broadband to 610 school districts. Priorities include enterprise AI governance, SNAP and Medicaid benefits modernization, and replacing 1970s-era data center infrastructure.

name: InnovateOhio Platform (Ohio Office of Information Technology)
description: Ohio's enterprise digital modernization initiative within the Department of Administrative Services' Office of Information Technology. Delivers OH|ID single sign-on (used by nearly half of Ohioans), data analytics, fraud detection, and a shared content platform for agency sites. Won a 2025 NASCIO State IT Recognition Award for cybersecurity.

name: Lebanon, NH
description: Small city with dedicated Chief Innovation & AI Officer. AI policy, procurement, training. Serves on NH AI Task Force.

name: Los Angeles Information Technology Agency (ITA)
description: City of Los Angeles enterprise technology department (442 staff, 366 services, ~$90M operating budget), ranked a top-two Digital City in 2023 and 2024. Published the LA AI Roadmap (2024) and a strategic plan covering AI governance and infrastructure for the 2026 World Cup and 2028 Olympics.
funding_detail: City of LA general fund; operating + capital budget appropriations

name: Maryland Digital Service & Office of AI Enablement
description: Digital service and AI delivery arm of the Maryland Department of Information Technology, created in 2024. Launched a bilingual AI assistant for SUN Bucks food benefits and co-leads a Rockefeller-backed AI partnership with Anthropic and Percepta on benefits, permitting, and housing. Published a 2025 AI Enablement Strategy.
funding_detail: MD state general fund; Anthropic/Percepta partnership; Rockefeller Foundation support

name: Massachusetts Digital Service (Mass Digital)
description: State digital service team within EOTSS implementing the Commonwealth Digital Roadmap. Built MyMassGov single sign-on (1.5M+ users) and the Ask MA multilingual chatbot, and announced ChatGPT for all 40K executive branch staff in 2026. Funded in part by the FutureTech Act of 2024 ($110M bond authorization).
funding_detail: MA state general fund + $110M FutureTech Act bond authorization

name: Minnesota IT Services (MNIT)
description: Enterprise IT agency serving 70+ Minnesota executive agencies and 87 counties. Launched LoginMN single sign-on, hired the state's first AI Director, and migrated 50%+ of servers to cloud. Its Technology Advisory Council guides AI, customer experience, and product-driven delivery.
funding_detail: State IT enterprise fund (chargeback model) + MN general fund appropriations

name: New Hampshire Department of Information Technology (DoIT)
description: Centralized state IT agency led since 2015 by Commissioner and CIO Denis Goulet (in role as of 2026). Redesigned state websites and apps, launched a statewide business portal, and runs '.Gov In a Box' to move local governments to .gov domains.
funding_detail: NH state general fund + federal SLCGP cybersecurity grants

name: New Jersey Innovation Authority (fmr. Office of Innovation)
description: State innovation team building digital products (Business.NJ.gov, NJ AI Assistant) and providing product, design, and data science support to NJ agencies. Codified in Jan 2026 as the New Jersey Innovation Authority within Treasury, the first state innovation team written into law.

name: New York State (ITS)
description: NY Office of Information Technology Services. Among 17+ states with official digital service teams per Beeck Center. Partnership with InnovateUS rolling out AI to 100K+ city employees.

name: North Carolina Digital Solutions
description: State digital services team within NC Department of Information Technology, operational since 2015.

name: NYC Office of Technology and Innovation (OTI)
description: New York City's consolidated technology agency, formed in 2022 from DoITT, Cyber Command, MODA, and other offices. About 1,200 staff and a ~$350M operating budget; runs NYC311, MyCity, and open data. CTO Lisa Gelobter appointed Feb 2026.

name: Orlando Digital Innovation and Service Design Team
description: Digital innovation and service design team within the City of Orlando IT department, operational since 2018. Verified active.

name: Philadelphia Digital Services
description: City digital team providing UX research, content strategy, and digital form development using USWDS.

name: Portland Digital Services (BTS)
description: City of Portland's in-house digital service team, launched in 2025, acting as design consultants to city bureaus on websites, apps, and permitting. Won USDR's Digital Champions Award (Nov 2025) and Code for America's Digital Transformation Award (May 2026) for permitting work; published a Digital Services Playbook in 2026.

name: Presidential Innovation Fellows (PIF)
description: Places mid-to-senior technologists in federal agencies for 12-month tours in product, AI strategy, design, and engineering (est. 2012; 260+ alumni). GSA named a 2026 cohort of 17 fellows serving 10 agencies.

name: Rhode Island Enterprise Technology Strategy and Services (ETSS)
description: Rhode Island enterprise technology and digital services team. Active 2024-2026 strategic plan.

name: San Diego Digital Experience Team
description: Digital experience team for the County of San Diego. Verified active with 1-5 FTE and 1 million budget.

name: San Francisco Digital and Data Services (DDS)
description: Human-centered digital service team in the City Administrator's office. Runs SF.gov (80+ departments migrated) under plain language and language access standards. Its Emerging Technologies team (Nov 2024) piloted ChatGPT Enterprise and deployed Microsoft Copilot Chat to 30,000 city staff.
funding_detail: City and County of San Francisco budget; COIT Major IT Project Allocation

name: San Jose Innovation & IT
description: City innovation team running data governance, AI strategy development, and employee upskilling. Leads GovAI coalition.

name: Seattle Information Technology (Seattle IT)
description: City of Seattle enterprise technology department (633+ staff, ~$280M operating budget). Its 2025-2027 Strategic Plan ties technology to public safety, housing, and health; launched Eproval permitting and the One Seattle Data Strategy. Runs the long-standing Technology Matching Fund digital equity grants.
funding_detail: City of Seattle general fund + capital budget

name: South Bend Division of Digital Services
description: Digital services team for the City of South Bend, Indiana. Established 2024. Verified active.

name: Syracuse Digital Services Division
description: Digital services division for the City of Syracuse, New York. Established 2022 with 6-10 FTE.

name: Technology Modernization Fund (TMF)
description: Federal revolving fund (Modernizing Government Technology Act, 2017) administered by GSA that provides milestone-based, repayable financing for agency IT modernization; GAO counts $1.03B across 68 unclassified projects at 40 agencies (FY2018-2025). funding_detail: Congressional appropriations ($5M FY26); agencies repay awards from savings and efficiencies generated

name: The Lab at OPM
description: Defunct (Apr 2025). Former OPM innovation lab (2012-2025) that pioneered human-centered design in the federal government and built HCD capacity across agencies.

name: U.S. Digital Corps
description: Two-year early-career federal fellowship (est. 2021) in software, data, product, design, and cybersecurity, run by GSA TTS. Paused: its largest cohort (2024) graduated in 2026, but no 2025 cohort was hired during the federal hiring freeze and no new cohort has been announced.

name: U.S. DOGE Service (fmr. USDS)
description: Formerly the U.S. Digital Service; renamed and reorganized under the DOGE executive order in Jan 2025, shifting its user-centered delivery mission toward software modernization. The DOGE temporary organization inside it ended July 4, 2026, but USDS continues, reporting about 90 staff and growing as of Apr 2026.

name: U.S. Tech Force (OPM)
description: OPM cross-agency hiring program launched Dec 2025 to place up to 1,000 early-career technologists a year in federal agencies for 1-2 year terms in AI, cybersecurity, data, and software. About 200 had been hired and were onboarding as of May 2026; NobleReach Foundation is the founding nonprofit partner.
funding_detail: Federal agency appropriations; centrally administered by OPM

name: Utah Digital Government
description: Utah's statewide digital government program. Launched a state digital ID (40K adopters in its first 3 months) and a personalized resident portal, and provides cybersecurity support to 100+ local entities.

name: Vermont Agency of Digital Services
description: Vermont statewide digital services agency. Active 2024 strategic plan.

name: Washington Technology Solutions (WaTech)
description: Washington State's central IT agency. Leads the Digital Experience program (Resident Portal roadmap), an AI Community of Practice, the state's first Enterprise Privacy and Data Protection Policy, and AI procurement guidelines. New CTO Gretchen Peri appointed Sept 2025.
funding_detail: WA state general fund + federal State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program funds

name: 120Water
description: Platform helping water utilities and agencies manage water safety testing, lead service line inventories, and EPA compliance, serving 1,300+ communities in 45+ states. Demand is driven by EPA Lead and Copper Rule Improvements requirements.
funding_detail: $57.6M total raised; $43M Series B (Jan 2024) led by Edison Partners; 1,300+ communities served

name: Binti
description: Child welfare software covering foster family recruitment and licensing, placements, case management, and prevention, usable as modules or a full CCWIS system. Sold to county and state agencies; used by 425+ agencies in 36 states and DC, including a statewide New York rollout.

name: Biobot Analytics
description: Wastewater intelligence platform (MIT origin) giving public health and national security agencies population-level data on disease and substance use. Contracts have included CDC's National Wastewater Surveillance System; selected by the White House Office of National Drug Control Policy for national substance use monitoring (Dec 2025).
funding_detail: Y Combinator; $20M Series A (2022); June 2025 round led by Valor Equity Partners with Atreides Management and Hyperplane

name: Bloom Housing (Exygy)
description: Open-source affordable housing portal built and stewarded by Exygy (B Corp), sold to city, county, and regional housing agencies. Powers DAHLIA (San Francisco) and Doorway (Bay Area Housing Finance Authority), handling lotteries, applications, waitlists, and reporting.
funding_detail: Government agency contracts (primary); Google.org pro bono support for specific deployments

name: Cambium AI
description: Population intelligence platform that integrates Census, IRS, CDC, housing, labor, and migration datasets into statistically grounded population models. Helps government and policy teams anticipate how populations will respond to programs before rollout. No PII; verified public data only.

name: Casebook PBC
description: Public benefit corporation, originally incubated by the Annie E. Casey Foundation, building case management software for child welfare, foster care, juvenile justice, and behavioral health agencies. 350+ customers; KPMG alliance for CCWIS modernization.
funding_detail: SaaS subscription revenue from government agencies and nonprofits; originally incubated by Annie E. Casey Foundation

name: Civic
description: AI-native platform for government constituent communications, casework management, and institutional knowledge. Serves congressional offices and state and local governments. Veteran-owned; seed-stage.
funding_detail: Pre-seed $1.3M from Analog Ventures, Center City Ventures, Wharton Venture Lab, Flybridge

name: Civic Roundtable
description: Operations platform for public servants that consolidates communication, documents, CRM, and AI-assisted knowledge retrieval for interagency work. Used by 4,000+ organizations across all 50 states. Founded 2022; backed by General Catalyst.

name: CivicReach
description: Voice AI agents that help understaffed local government offices and call centers answer resident calls at more hours and in more languages, handling routine questions so staff can focus on complex cases. Clients include the City of Memphis and Virginia Community Action Partnership.
funding_detail: Pre-seed (Nov 2025, undisclosed) from Flybridge, Triangle Tweener Fund, and CivStart; ~$310K raised previously incl. NC IDEA

name: CiviForm
description: Open-source benefits application platform built by the City of Seattle with Google.org Fellows and Exygy, now used by Seattle, Charlotte, Bloomington IN, Arkansas, and Miami-Dade. Residents apply for several programs at once; agencies build forms in a no-code tool without vendor lock-in.
funding_detail: Google.org grant funding to Exygy; free and open-source for adopting governments; Seed/Early stage

name: Cyvl.ai
description: Vehicle-mounted sensors and AI that map and assess roads, sidewalks, signs, and other assets so public works departments and DOTs can plan repairs. Partners with 100+ local governments.
funding_detail: ~$23M total raised; $14M Series A (Oct 2025) led by Sentinel Global; $6M round (Mar 2024) led by Companyon Ventures

name: Daupler
description: AI response management platform for utilities and public works departments that triages incidents such as water main breaks and dispatches crews. Serves utilities in 38 states, Canada, and New Zealand; expanding to the UK and EU.
funding_detail: $15M Series B (Mar 2025) led by Aqualateral with Burnt Island Ventures and KCRise Fund

name: Democracy Works
description: Nonprofit building voting technology for election officials and voters. Voting Information Project (VIP) gives election offices a free platform to share official voting location and ballot data with voters through Google Civic API and major platforms. 40+ state and DC partners.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Knight Foundation, Democracy Fund; philanthropic grants

name: Digital Public Works
description: Nonprofit govtech founded by former USDS staff. Its first product is a consent-based income verification tool that lets benefits applicants share payroll data directly with state agencies; states are the primary customer.

name: GovWell
description: Software for government permitting, licensing, and code enforcement, sold directly to local building, planning, fire, and public works departments. Serves 130+ municipalities and counties in 34 states as of 2026.
funding_detail: $34.5M total raised; $25M Series A (May 2026) led by Insight Partners; prior seed from Work-Bench, Bienville Capital, Fractal Software

name: Holly
description: AI-powered platform modernizing government hiring. Automates job description creation with 45,000+ templates, provides real-time salary benchmarking, and reduces government hiring cycles that average 135 days. Addresses ~1M vacant government positions nationwide.
funding_detail: $2.2M pre-seed (Jan 2025) led by J2 Ventures; Roble Ventures, Gaingels

name: Marketplace.city
description: Market intelligence and procurement platform helping state and local governments research vendors, compare contracts and pricing, and procure technology (Clearbox Source and Clearbox Procure). Grew out of NYC's Marketplace.NYC; government procurement offices are the primary customer.

name: PayIt
description: Digital payments and services platform for resident transactions with government (DMV, property tax, utilities), funded by transaction fees often at no cost to the agency. Serves 100M+ residents in North America; GovTech 100 honoree seven years running.
funding_detail: Insight Partners, Weatherford Capital; $190M+ total raised; transaction fee model

name: Peregrine Technologies
description: Real-time data platform that helps public safety and government agencies unify siloed data for decisions across law enforcement, emergency response, and fraud detection. Serves agencies covering 80M+ Americans; supported multi-agency operations at Super Bowl LIX.
funding_detail: $220M total raised; $190M Series C (Mar 2025) led by Sequoia Capital at $2.5B valuation; prior $30M Series B (May 2024)

name: Polco
description: Civic engagement and performance analytics platform for local government, including the National Community Survey (via its NRC acquisition), resident polling, and Balancing Act budget simulations. Used by 1,000+ communities.
funding_detail: ~$22.5M total raised; $14M round (Oct 2022) led by Mercury Fund with BAT Ventures and Royal Street Ventures

name: Polimorphic
description: AI platform for local government service delivery, from resident intake through resolution. Products include AI Front Desk (multilingual constituent service in 75+ languages), a Constituent Relationship Manager, and analytics; serves cities and counties in multiple states.
funding_detail: VC-backed; $28M total raised including $18.6M Series A led by General Catalyst (2025); M13 and Shine also investors

name: Promise
description: Modernizes government payment and collections systems, helping agencies recover revenue while giving residents flexible, humane payment options. Sells directly to government billing departments.
funding_detail: ~$48M total raised; $25M Series B (Feb 2022) led by The General Partnership; Series A led by Kapor Capital and XYZ; Y Combinator (S19)

name: Propel
description: Free app used by about 5 million SNAP households to check EBT balances and find grocery savings; revenue comes from coupons and partners, not government. Runs the Propel AI Residency, pairing former state SNAP and Medicaid leaders with engineers on tools for agencies.
funding_detail: $50M Series B (2022); ~$50M ARR; $3.5M Gates Foundation grant for AI safety-net navigation tools

name: Recidiviz
description: Data and technology platform for corrections agencies. Products include supervision tools, caseload management, and data infrastructure for state departments of corrections. Government is the primary paying customer.
funding_detail: Arnold Ventures, Schmidt Futures; state agency contracts

name: SimpliGov
description: No-code workflow automation platform purpose-built for government, digitizing paper-based processes like licensing, permits, HR onboarding, and constituent requests. Clients include federal agencies and state/local governments.
funding_detail: JMI Equity strategic growth investment (Jan 2025; undisclosed amount)

name: Syncurrent
description: AI grant discovery and application platform for local and tribal governments, cutting months of manual work to minutes. Active in 200+ governments on a subscription model.
funding_detail: Subscription revenue plus enterprise agreements; VC-backed (early stage)

name: Zencity
description: AI community insights platform helping local governments understand resident sentiment, measure service satisfaction, and run public engagement. Serves 400+ governments, including NYC, Dallas, and LAPD; acquired UK engagement platform Commonplace in Jan 2025.
funding_detail: $91M total raised; $40M Series C (Jun 2024) led by StepStone Group; prior investors TLV Partners, Salesforce Ventures, M12 (Microsoft)

name: 8VC (Joe Lonsdale)
description: Venture firm with an explicit govtech and defense thesis, co-founded by Joe Lonsdale. Co-founded and backed OpenGov (acquired by Cox Enterprises for $1.8B in 2024).
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; $6B+ AUM across multiple funds

name: Advantage Capital / InState Partners
description: St. Louis-based impact investor whose InState Partners line (est. 2013) invests in govtech, pairing capital with a 50-state government affairs network to navigate procurement. First investor in PayIt; three-year strategic partnership with CivStart.
funding_detail: Tax credit-driven funds + traditional LP capital; $4B+ total deployed; InState Partners is dedicated govtech line

name: America's Frontier Fund
description: Nonprofit strategic investment fund for frontier technologies (semiconductors, AI, quantum, advanced manufacturing) tied to US security and competitiveness. Led by Gilman Louie (former In-Q-Tel CEO), with Jennifer Pahlka on its board; DoD SBICCT partner.
funding_detail: Private capital; DoD SBICCT program; philanthropic contributions

name: Andreessen Horowitz
description: Major VC whose American Dynamism practice backs defense and government technology startups. Govtech investments include OpenGov (sold to Cox for $1.8B in 2024), Flock Safety, and Skydio; defense and national security dominate the portfolio.
funding_detail: LP-funded; $42B+ AUM; American Dynamism Fund dedicated to defense and government tech

name: BarronKent Ventures
description: Sacramento-based family office and early-stage VC with an explicit govtech focus, founded by principals who ran a national govtech consulting firm for 18 years. Invests across HHS, transportation and tolling, licensing, and government finance systems; active in the CivStart ecosystem.
funding_detail: Family office + LP-funded VC; undisclosed fund size; early to growth stage

name: Blue Ridge Labs (Robin Hood Foundation)
description: Social impact venture studio within the Robin Hood Foundation that builds and funds early-stage startups serving low-income New Yorkers. Several portfolio companies work directly with NYC agencies on service delivery.

name: BV Investment Partners
description: Boston-based middle-market PE firm with government technology as a named sector. Made a minority investment in CivicPlus in 2019 and scaled it before a $290M exit to Insight Partners in 2021.
funding_detail: LP-funded PE; ~$3.9B total invested since 1983; govtech is named sector focus

name: Commonweal Ventures
description: Early-stage VC founded in 2022 by former Obama White House adviser Nate Loewentheil, backing startups whose growth runs through government as buyer, funder, or regulator. Portfolio includes Multitude Insights, Deckard Technologies, and Advocate (benefits applications); participated in Starbridge's Series A (2025).
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; $500K-$2.5M pre-seed and seed checks; Empire State Development (New York Ventures) is an LP

name: Govtech Fund (Ron Bouganim)
description: First VC fund dedicated to govtech, founded by Ron Bouganim; makes $250K-$500K seed investments in companies selling to government (~$50M across two funds). Portfolio includes Mark43, SeamlessDocs/GovOS, SmartProcure, and Merit.
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; ~$50M AUM across two funds; seed stage ($250K-$500K checks)

name: Govtech Ventures (Rachel Stern)
description: Solo-GP early-stage VC fund (est. 2024) dedicated to state and local government, founded by Rachel Stern, first investor in PayIt and co-founder of InState Partners. Has held a first close on a $15M inaugural fund for pre-seed and seed checks; portfolio includes Polco, Streamline, Ladris, and Madison AI.
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; $15M inaugural fund (first close achieved); pre-seed to seed-plus stage

name: Great Hill Partners
description: Boston-based PE firm with a deliberate govtech strategy, sourcing deals with Granicus co-founder Tom Spengler as Executive-in-Residence. Led the 2025 majority recapitalization of Vision Government Solutions (property tax software, 900+ jurisdictions) with Weatherford Capital.
funding_detail: LP-funded PE; $12B+ total capital raised across funds; govtech is named vertical

name: IQT (In-Q-Tel)
description: Strategic investor for the US intelligence community, founded by the CIA in 1999. Invests in commercial AI, cybersecurity, data analytics, and quantum companies to bring their capabilities to national security agencies.
funding_detail: CIA and US intelligence community funding

name: J2 Ventures
description: Venture fund investing in software and technology for defense, national security, and other government customers. Also backs state and local govtech, including leading Holly's pre-seed round (Jan 2025).

name: JFF Ventures
description: Impact venture arm of Jobs for the Future, investing in workforce and education technology where public workforce programs (WIOA, Perkins) are often the primary customer. Links JFF's policy and research work to technology investment.

name: Kapor Capital
description: Oakland-based early-stage VC (est. 1999) investing in startups that close access gaps for low-income communities and communities of color. Govtech investments include Promise and Aclima.
funding_detail: LP-funded VC; $126M Fund III (Sept 2022), its first with outside LPs; pre-seed and seed focus

name: Omidyar Network
description: Philanthropic investment firm making grants and equity investments in responsible technology and governance, with $2B+ deployed to 700+ organizations. Funds TechCongress; spun out Luminate as a separate grantmaking entity.
funding_detail: Pierre and Pam Omidyar personal capital; ~$2B deployed across grants and equity investments

name: Paladin Capital Group
description: Washington DC-based VC investing in cybersecurity and critical infrastructure protection companies whose primary customers are government and defense, including DHS, DoD, and civilian agencies.

name: Serent Capital
description: Growth PE firm with a dedicated govtech team investing in profitable SaaS for state and local agencies. Portfolio includes BS&A Software (municipal ERP), First Due (fire and EMS), GovWorx (911 quality assurance), and Pondera Solutions (benefits fraud detection, sold to Thomson Reuters).
funding_detail: LP-funded PE; multiple funds since 2008; $3B+ total capital under management

name: Socium Ventures
description: Evergreen venture fund backed by Cox Enterprises, with $600M+ committed across two funds. Govtech investments include Carbyne (911 platform, acquired by Axon for $625M in Nov 2025); parent Cox acquired OpenGov in 2024.
funding_detail: Cox Enterprises-backed evergreen fund; $300M Fund II (Oct 2024); $600M+ total committed

name: Town Hall Ventures
description: Healthcare VC founded in 2018 by former CMS acting administrator Andy Slavitt and David Whelan, backing companies that improve care for Medicare, Medicaid, and other underserved populations. Closed a $440M Fund IV in Oct 2025 focused on AI-enabled care.

name: Weatherford Capital (Will Weatherford)
description: Family-owned PE firm founded in 2015 by former Florida House Speaker Will Weatherford. Seven govtech platform investments, including PayIt, OpenGov (sold to Cox for $1.8B in 2024), SOMA Global, and BusPatrol; closed a $300M Fund II in 2025.
funding_detail: Family-owned PE; $300M Fund II closed 2025; $1B+ AUM across two funds

name: Annie E. Casey Foundation
description: Major funder of Georgetown Beeck Center. Focus on child welfare, juvenile justice, and family economic success; all areas where government delivery capacity is critical. name: Arnold Ventures
description: Funds evidence-based government reform including Results for America and government performance initiatives. Focus on criminal justice, health, evidence-based implementation.

name: Ballmer Group (Steve & Connie Ballmer)
description: Funds data-driven systems change for economic mobility, including evidence-based government, workforce development, and government data use. Key funder of GovEx/JHU Centers for Civic Impact and USAFacts, co-founder of NextLadder Ventures, and funding partner of the Public Benefit Innovation Fund; $1B+ commitment to Washington State early childhood.
funding_detail: Steve Ballmer personal wealth (fmr. Microsoft CEO)

name: Bloomberg Philanthropies: Government Innovation
