name: Blue Meridian Partners
description: Funder collaborative that finds and scales solutions for economic mobility, with Ballmer Group as a major partner. Many grantees work directly with government on benefits delivery, workforce development, and child welfare systems.
funding_detail: Ballmer Group, Sergey Brin Family Foundation, Edna McConnell Clark Foundation + others; grants-based, not equity

name: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI)
description: LLC blending grants and investments; funded FUSE Corps and Bay Area housing, health, and economic development programs. Restructured in Feb 2025 away from social advocacy toward AI in science and education, narrowing its state capacity relevance.
funding_detail: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan personal wealth; operates as LLC

name: Craig Newmark Philanthropies
description: Foundation of craigslist founder Craig Newmark. Major funder of Aspen Policy Academy since its founding; supports cybersecurity, trustworthy journalism, and the public interest technology pipeline.

name: Data.org
description: Nonprofit building the field of data for social impact. Capacity Accelerator Network provides training and resources for organizations using data to improve public services. Inclusive Growth and Recovery Challenge funds data-driven solutions.
funding_detail: Mastercard Center for Inclusive Growth + philanthropic

name: de Beaumont Foundation
description: Private foundation (est. 1998) that strengthens state and local health department capacity and the public health workforce as an engaged funder that does not take unsolicited proposals. Programs include the PH WINS workforce survey (with ASTHO), Public Health Forward (with Bipartisan Policy Center), and the Public Health Workforce Calculator.
funding_detail: Fully endowed private foundation (Pierre de Beaumont estate); does not accept unsolicited proposals

name: Democracy Fund (Omidyar Group)
description: Nonpartisan foundation with effective and accountable government as one of four pillars, making 200+ grants a year. Funds congressional modernization (POPVOX Foundation, Lincoln Network), government transparency, and legislative branch capacity; shifted toward democracy defense in 2025-2026.
funding_detail: Pierre and Pam Omidyar / Omidyar Group

name: Emerson Collective (Laurene Powell Jobs)
description: LLC founded by Laurene Powell Jobs blending venture, philanthropy, and advocacy. Invested in OpenGov; works to reshape government systems in education and immigration and founded Chicago CRED and E Pluribus Unum.
funding_detail: Powell Jobs personal wealth; Waverley Street Foundation committed $3.5B over 10 years

name: Families and Workers Fund
description: $135M+ pooled funder collaborative (40+ funders) supporting public benefits delivery modernization, civic tech, and government innovation alongside workforce policy. Funding partner of the Public Benefit Innovation Fund, housed at the Center for Civic Futures.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Schmidt Futures, Rockefeller Foundation, Annie E. Casey, Open Society Foundations, MacKenzie Scott, and 35+ co-funders

name: Ford Foundation
description: Major funder of public interest technology ecosystem. Co-convenes PIT-UN. Funds Coding it Forward, FUSE Corps, Aspen Policy Academy, Data & Society, Ash Center endowment, PIT Infrastructure Fund.

name: Gates Foundation
description: Funds GovEx/JHU Centers for Civic Impact and government data capacity in public health and education. Co-founder of NextLadder Ventures and funding partner of the Public Benefit Innovation Fund; government modernization is secondary to its core programs.

name: Google.org
description: Google's philanthropic arm, funding AI for social good, digital skills, and civic technology. Funded Decoded Futures ($1M), InnovateUS ($5M, 2025), and CiviForm through Google.org Fellows.

name: Hewlett Foundation
description: Co-convenes PIT-UN. Funds TechCongress, public interest technology infrastructure, and government performance programs.

name: Irvine Foundation (James Irvine Foundation)
description: California-focused funder. Supports FUSE Corps. Focus on economic and political inclusion in California; funds orgs that strengthen civic participation and government responsiveness at state and local levels.

name: Knight Foundation
description: Funds civic engagement, data-driven governance, and smart city strategies, with a focus on mid-size US cities. Grantees include Harvard Data-Smart City Solutions, GovEx/JHU, and San Jose AI partnerships; runs the Knight Emerging City Champions fellowship.

name: Luminate (Omidyar Group)
description: Global foundation spun out of Omidyar Network in 2018, funding civic empowerment, data and digital rights, financial transparency, and independent media. Exited its domestic US grantmaking by the end of 2023; now focuses on Latin America, Africa, Southeast Asia, and Europe.
funding_detail: Pierre and Pam Omidyar / Omidyar Group

name: MacArthur Foundation
description: Major funder of Civic Consulting Alliance ($6M+ since 2003). Supports government accountability, criminal justice reform, and community development orgs that work with local government. Also funds Data & Society and investigative journalism that surfaces government capacity issues.

name: Mastercard Center for Inclusive Growth / Mastercard Impact Fund
description: Mastercard's corporate philanthropy arm. Co-funds PIT-UN with Ford and Hewlett, funds data.org, and supports digital inclusion and financial access programs with governments.

name: New Profit
description: Venture philanthropy fund (since 1998) backing social entrepreneurs in civic engagement and government service delivery. Build Investments provide $1.5M multi-year unrestricted grants; portfolio includes public service pipeline orgs such as Latinas Represent.

name: NextLadder Ventures
description: $1B+ initiative launched July 2025 by Ballmer Group, Gates Foundation, Stand Together, Valhalla Foundation, and John Overdeck. Invests in entrepreneurs building tools that help low-income Americans navigate government systems, using grants, equity, and revenue-based financing over 15 years.
funding_detail: $1B+ committed across founding coalition over 15 years; mix of grants, equity, and revenue-based financing

name: Coefficient Giving (fmr. Open Philanthropy)
description: Renamed from Open Philanthropy in Nov 2025 as it expanded into multi-donor funds alongside Good Ventures. Major funder of Niskanen Center's state capacity work and evidence-based policy research. Runs collaborative funds including the Abundance and Growth Fund.
funding_detail: Good Ventures (Cari Tuna and Dustin Moskovitz) plus multi-donor funds

name: Patrick J. McGovern Foundation
description: Co-funds PIT Infrastructure Fund. Supports Coding it Forward, Govern for America, and orgs advancing responsible AI and data use in public sector.

name: Pivotal Ventures (Melinda French Gates)
description: Co-funds PIT Infrastructure Fund. Supports Coding it Forward, Govern for America, and pathways for underrepresented technologists in government.

name: Public Benefit Innovation Fund
description: Pooled grantmaking vehicle housed at the Center for Civic Futures that funds states and their partners to develop AI tools for public benefits delivery. Awarded $8.5M to eight projects in Dec 2025.
funding_detail: Ballmer Group, Gates Foundation, W.K. Kellogg Foundation, Renaissance Philanthropy, Families and Workers Fund; Digital Harbor Foundation

name: Public Interest Technology Infrastructure Fund (PIT Fund)
description: Pooled grantmaking vehicle housed at New Venture Fund. Dedicated to building the PIT ecosystem; funds talent pipeline orgs like Coding it Forward ($550K), Govern for America, #BlackTechFutures ($250K), AAAS AI fellowships ($250K), PIT hubs ($200K each), and Data & Society. Funded by Ford, Siegel, McGovern, Pivotal, Schmidt Futures.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Siegel, McGovern, Pivotal Ventures, Schmidt Futures

name: Raikes Foundation
description: Co-funds PIT-UN. Founded by Jeff Raikes (fmr. Microsoft exec, fmr. Gates Foundation CEO). Supports education, youth development, and public interest technology pipeline programs.

name: Robin Hood Foundation
description: NYC's largest local poverty-fighting philanthropy. Seeded Decoded Futures AI capacity-building for nonprofits delivering public services.

name: Rockefeller Foundation
description: Launched AI Readiness Project (Nov 2025) expanding to all 50 states. Funds state/local government AI capacity-building and digital inclusion.

name: Schmidt Futures
description: Philanthropic initiative of Eric and Wendy Schmidt that made grants and investments in talent and technology, funding USDR, FAS, PIT-UN, and benefits access modernization. Restructured from Oct 2023 into more focused organizations; its science programs now run under Schmidt Sciences.
funding_detail: Schmidt family wealth; operates as LLC

name: Siegel Family Endowment
description: Committed $20M to PIT ecosystem. Co-funds PIT Infrastructure Fund. Supports Coding it Forward, Aspen Policy Academy, Data & Society, New America PIT.

name: Thierer Family Foundation
description: Chicago-based foundation funding technology capacity for nonprofits and government-adjacent organizations. Founded Vivery, a food access platform used by 21+ food banks, and provides it to nonprofits at no cost.

name: Valhalla Foundation
description: Foundation focused on children's outcomes through early childhood, K-12 education, and data science. Co-founder of NextLadder Ventures; funds data-driven improvement of government-run education and child welfare systems.

name: AI Now Institute of Technology
description: Independent policy research institute (est. 2017 at NYU) studying AI's social implications, power concentration, and government use of AI in benefits, hiring, and criminal justice. Publishes the annual AI Now Landscape Report. Refuses corporate tech funding.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Open Society Foundations, Omidyar Network, Luminate; no corporate tech industry funding

name: Aspen Institute
description: Nonpartisan leadership and policy forum. State capacity-relevant programs include Aspen Policy Academy (listed separately) and Aspen Digital (technology policy), plus governance convenings.
funding_detail: Broad philanthropic base; major foundation support; event revenue

name: Bipartisan Policy Center (BPC)
description: Centrist think tank founded by former Senate majority leaders from both parties. Governance program focuses on congressional capacity, executive branch management, and government modernization. Technology project examines AI governance and digital government policy.
funding_detail: Bipartisan philanthropic base; foundation and corporate support

name: Brookings: Center for Technology Innovation
description: Policy research on AI governance, digital government, tech talent, and government modernization. Congressional testimony.

name: Building State Capability (BSC) - Harvard Kennedy School
description: Harvard Kennedy School program led by Matt Andrews that developed Problem Driven Iterative Adaptation (PDIA) for escaping government capability traps. Has trained 4,850+ practitioners in 157 countries through online courses, executive education, and coaching.
funding_detail: Harvard Kennedy School endowment + earned revenue from executive education

name: Center for a New American Security (CNAS)
description: Bipartisan national security think tank. Technology and National Security program researches AI, emerging tech, and defense innovation. [NOTE: Primarily defense-focused. State capacity relevance is limited to where defense tech/AI governance intersects with broader government modernization.]
funding_detail: Broad bipartisan donor base; foundation and government grants

name: Center for Democracy and Technology (CDT)
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit (est. 1994) shaping technology policy around individual rights. Its AI Governance Lab (launched 2023) advises policymakers and agencies on AI auditing, documentation, and government use of AI in benefits, education, and law enforcement.
funding_detail: Foundation-funded; Ford Foundation, Open Society Foundations, and others; no corporate tech funding

name: Center for Information Technology Policy (CITP, Princeton)
description: Princeton interdisciplinary research center on technology and public life, covering election security, AI regulation, algorithmic accountability, and digital rights. Alumni pipeline into USDS, FTC, and congressional tech policy roles.

name: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET)
description: Georgetown think tank focused on AI and national security policy, producing analysis for DoD, Congress, and the intelligence community. Founded by former IARPA director Jason Matheny.
funding_detail: Coefficient Giving (fmr. Open Philanthropy) (primary funder); Georgetown University

name: Center for Tribal Digital Sovereignty (ASU / NCAI)
description: First US center helping tribal governments build digital sovereignty plans, launched June 2024 by ASU Law's American Indian Policy Institute and the National Congress of American Indians. Provides research and capacity-building on broadband, data, spectrum, and AI governance; co-hosts the Wiring the Rez conference.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation + Google.org seed funding; ASU and NCAI foundational support; seeking additional philanthropic partners

name: Centre for Public Impact (CPI)
description: Global not-for-profit providing government reimagining consulting, adaptive leadership coaching, and legitimacy frameworks.
funding_detail: BCG Foundation (founded by BCG; now independently operated); diversified philanthropic base

name: Council of State Governments (CSG)
description: Nonpartisan organization (est. 1933) serving all three branches of state government through six regional offices. Publishes the Book of the States and the CSG 50-State Scan (2025); the CSG Justice Center develops criminal justice reform strategies.
funding_detail: State appropriations (population-based dues) + federal grants + foundation grants

name: Data & Society
description: Research institute studying social implications of data and AI. Public Technology Leadership Collaborative connects tech experts with government leaders.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, MacArthur Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment

name: Data Foundation
description: Nonprofit that tracks open government data policy across all 50 states and publishes the annual State of Data Ownership report. Runs the Data Coalition, advocating for federal and state data infrastructure standards. Meaningful node for open data and data infrastructure problem statements.
funding_detail: Foundation grants; member dues from Data Coalition

name: Foundation for American Innovation
description: Center-right innovation policy think tank whose Senior Fellows program places technologists in congressional offices. Work includes GAO reform, AI governance, and congressional tech capacity; runs the AI Policy Leadership Network with CNAS and Horizon.

name: Georgetown Beeck Center
description: Provides technical assistance, communities of practice, and practitioner training on digital government, data, and AI for state and local agencies. In 2026 merged its Digital Benefits, Digital Service, and State CDO networks into the Digital Government Network; runs the Digital Government Hub.
funding_detail: Georgetown + Annie E. Casey Foundation, Bloomberg, others

name: Government Finance Officers Association (GFOA)
description: Professional association (est. 1906) of 30,000+ state, provincial, and local government finance officers; publishes the GAAFR Blue Book and runs budget and reporting award programs. Its Research and Consulting Center has helped 450+ governments select and negotiate ERP and financial systems.
funding_detail: Member dues + conference revenue + consulting fees + publication sales

name: GovEx / Johns Hopkins Centers for Civic Impact
description: Bloomberg Center for Government Excellence at Johns Hopkins, providing technical assistance, coaching, and training to help cities use data, analytics, and AI. Runs City Data Alliance programming, GovEx Academy, and a CDOs-in-Residence program; has worked with 140+ cities.
funding_detail: Bloomberg Philanthropies, Ballmer Group, Knight Foundation, Gates Foundation + JHU

name: Harvard Ash Center for Democratic Governance and Innovation
description: Harvard Kennedy School center for government innovation and democratic governance, supported by a $50M Ford Foundation endowment. Runs the Innovations in American Government Awards (since 1985), Data-Smart City Solutions, and the Allen Lab for Democracy Renovation. Houses the Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative.
funding_detail: $50M Ford Foundation endowment + Bloomberg Philanthropies ($32M for City Leadership Initiative) + Harvard Kennedy School

name: IBM Center for the Business of Government
description: Research center (est. 1998; part of IBM since 2002) funding practitioner-focused research on federal, state, and local public management. Publishes 25+ reports a year on digital modernization, AI adoption, workforce, procurement, and administrative burden.

name: Information Technology and Innovation Foundation (ITIF)
description: Nonpartisan science and tech policy think tank. Research on government IT modernization, AI policy, and digital infrastructure. Published 'After DOGE: Trump's Chance to Modernize.'

name: Institute for Progress (IFP)
description: The Institute for Progress (IFP) is a nonpartisan think tank founded 2022 focused on innovation policy: metascience, immigration, emerging technology, and AI infrastructure. Provides technical assistance to federal agencies and runs Capitol Hill briefings for congressional staff. Produces rapid-turnaround policy analysis on high-stakes technology and science policy questions.
funding_detail: Arnold Ventures, Sloan Foundation, Schmidt Futures, Coefficient Giving (fmr. Open Philanthropy), Astera Foundation

name: Jain Family Institute
description: Nonpartisan applied research organization (est. 2014) advising cities, state legislatures, and federal policymakers. Work spans guaranteed income program design (Compton Pledge, Stockton SEED), digital ethics and AI governance, and macroeconomic policy.
funding_detail: Private foundation funding (Bobby Jain); Open Society Foundations

name: J-PAL North America
description: MIT-based research center running randomized evaluations with state and local governments. Its State and Local Innovation Initiative and LEVER Evaluation Incubator (with Results for America) help agencies generate evidence on housing, criminal justice, workforce, health, and education. Has partnered with 18+ state and local governments since 2015.
funding_detail: Arnold Ventures, Gates Foundation, JPB Foundation, federal research grants

name: Manhattan Institute
description: Center-right think tank on urban policy and public-sector reform, with a governance program focused on transparency, accountability, and evidence-based reform. Publishes City Journal and 'Digital Transformation: Wiring the Responsive City.'
funding_detail: Conservative philanthropic base; individual and foundation donors

name: MDRC
description: Nonprofit research organization (est. 1974) specializing in randomized evaluations of social and education programs. Works directly with government agencies on program design and evaluation; multi-year Arnold Ventures partner.
funding_detail: Arnold Ventures (multi-year); Annie E. Casey, Rockefeller; government agency contracts

name: Mercatus Center (George Mason University)
description: George Mason University research center focused on regulatory reform, permitting modernization, and government process improvement, including influential work on regulatory accumulation. Also runs a technology policy program.
funding_detail: George Mason University + Koch-affiliated and broad donor base

name: MIT GOV/LAB
description: Research lab studying government innovation, political accountability, and institutional design using field experiments and design thinking.

name: National Association of Counties (NACo)
description: The only national organization representing all 3,069 US county governments. Runs the County Tech Xchange peer network for county CIOs, published the AI County Compass governance guide (2024), and hosts regional AI forums. Complementary to NLC which covers municipalities; NACo covers the county layer of government.

name: National Civic League
description: Nonpartisan nonprofit (est. 1894) promoting civic engagement and government innovation. All-America City Award (oldest community recognition in US). Research on collaborative governance, civic infrastructure, and democratic innovation.

name: National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL)
description: Bipartisan organization serving 7,500+ state legislators and staff across all states and territories. Provides nonpartisan research, technical assistance, and legislative tracking, including AI (450+ bills tracked in 2024), cybersecurity, broadband, and digital government.
funding_detail: State legislative appropriations (member dues) + federal grants + foundation grants

name: National League of Cities (NLC)
description: Membership and research organization representing 19,000+ cities, towns, and villages. Publishes the annual State of the Cities report and digital government research, partners with the Beeck Center on digital services guidance, and co-hosts State of GovTech with CivStart.
funding_detail: City membership dues + foundation grants + federal grants

name: New America: Public Interest Technology
description: PIT program: fellowships, The Commons (procurement research), policy research. Co-convenes PIT University Network (PIT-UN): 63 institutions, $16M+ deployed.
funding_detail: Ford Foundation, Hewlett Foundation, Siegel Family Endowment

name: NGA Center for Best Practices
description: R&D arm of the National Governors Association, providing policy analysis and direct technical assistance to governors' offices across five divisions. Runs policy academies for state teams on implementation challenges such as SNAP E&T delivery and workforce pathways.
funding_detail: State appropriations (population-based dues) + federal grants + foundation support

name: Niskanen Center: Project on State Capacity
description: Dedicated state capacity research initiative. Published 'The How We Need Now' capacity agenda. Policy research on civil service reform, digital modernization, product operating model, implementation-focused legislation.
funding_detail: Coefficient Giving (fmr. Open Philanthropy), broad donor base

name: Pew Charitable Trusts: Government Performance
description: Nonpartisan research organization whose state government work produces empirical research on state fiscal health, budgeting, and government performance. Its Fiscal 50 platform tracks revenue, spending, and reserves in all 50 states.
funding_detail: $7B+ endowment; earned revenue from research contracts

name: Progressive Policy Institute (PPI)
description: Center-left think tank in the New Democrat tradition with a technology and innovation program. Research covers government digital transformation, broadband, AI policy, and building state capacity through technology.

name: R Street Institute
description: Free-market think tank producing research on limited, effective government, regulatory reform, and tech policy.

name: RAND Corporation
description: Nonpartisan research institute that also consults directly for government. Its Center on AI, Security & Technology researches AI policy, including scaling AI in state and local government; founding partner of PIT-UN.
funding_detail: Coefficient Giving (fmr. Open Philanthropy), government contracts, endowment, broad donor base

name: RegLab (Stanford)
description: Stanford lab partnering with agencies such as IRS, EPA, DOL, and Santa Clara County to design and evaluate AI and data science for core governance functions. Known for its IRS audit disparity analysis; also runs talent pipeline programs into the public sector.
funding_detail: Stanford Impact Labs (3.5M, 4-year); government agency partnerships

name: Responsible AI Institute (RAI Institute)
description: Independent nonprofit providing AI certification, conformity assessments, and responsible AI tools for government agencies. Develops standards and frameworks for trustworthy AI procurement and deployment.

name: Roosevelt Institute
description: Left-of-center think tank focused on economic policy and government capacity research. Primary output is policy research on public investment, industrial policy, and government effectiveness. Student network is a separate affiliated entity.

name: Searchlight Institute
description: A Democratic-aligned policy think tank focused on reshaping the party's strategy toward broader, more electorally viable positions.

name: Stanford Digital Economy Lab
description: Research on technology's impact on economy, work, and institutions (Erik Brynjolfsson). Quantitative research on AI economics and labor markets.

name: Stanford HAI (Human-Centered AI Institute)
description: Stanford institute studying AI's social, ethical, and governance implications; publishes the annual AI Index. Runs AI policy fellowships that place researchers with government and engages Congress and OMB on federal AI policy.
funding_detail: Stanford University; HAI industry partners; foundation grants

name: The GovLab (NYU Tandon + Burnes Center at Northeastern)
description: Research lab studying how technology and data improve governance. Open data, data collaboratives, collective intelligence, and citizen engagement.

name: Urban Institute
description: Nonpartisan social and economic policy research organization. Research covers government finance, safety net delivery, benefits modernization, and evidence-based implementation, with data tools for policymakers.
funding_detail: Foundation grants + government research contracts + endowment

name: Volcker Alliance
description: Nonprofit (est. 2014 by Paul Volcker) working on public service education, public sector talent, and public finance, including state budget integrity research. Runs the Tech to Gov hiring forum, Public Service Ambassadors, and the NextGen Service student network.

name: Yale Tobin Center for Economic Policy
description: Domestic policy center providing direct technical assistance to governments and multi-university research partnerships on evidence-based policy.

name: We the Doers
description: A nonpartisan organization of former senior federal career civil servants producing practical reform recommendations for agency leaders, the executive branch, and Congress. Founded December 2025. Focused on removing structural barriers to effective service delivery.
funding_detail: No public funding disclosure as of June 2026.

name: ClearGov
description: Cloud budget cycle management software for local governments, school districts, and state agencies, covering capital, personnel, and operating budgets, digital budget books, and reporting. Acquired by Lead Edge Capital in Jan 2026 and merged with Gravity; the combined company operates as ClearGov.
funding_detail: Acquired by Lead Edge Capital (Jan 2026) and merged with Gravity; previously a $20M growth round (Jan 2022) led by Frontier Growth

name: DebtBook
description: Treasury management platform purpose-built for government and nonprofit finance teams. Automates GASB 87/96 compliance, ACFR note generation, debt tracking, and cash positioning in a single system. Used by 40% of the 250 largest U.S. municipalities and counties; 2,100+ customers nationwide.
funding_detail: Privately held; no publicly disclosed external funding; legal entity is Fifth Asset Inc.

name: BondLink
description: Investor relations and debt management platform for municipal bond issuers, helping state and local governments communicate with investors, manage disclosure, and run bond sales. Supported $100B+ in client par in 2025 and connects issuers to the Bloomberg Terminal; GovTech 100 eight years running.
funding_detail: $34.1M total raised across 4 rounds; Series B (2021); investors include Intercontinental Exchange and Franklin Templeton

name: Hazel
description: AI procurement software for government that automates solicitation drafting, vendor matching, compliance checks, and proposal evaluation, with procurement officers retaining final decisions. Customers range from school districts to the U.S. Navy; YC W2024.
funding_detail: Y Combinator (W2024); seed stage; total undisclosed

name: Cardinality.ai
description: Pre-built, low-code AI platform for health and human services agencies covering child welfare, child support, SNAP, TANF, Medicaid, and workforce programs. Serves 11 agencies in 5 states, reaching 23M+ constituents.
funding_detail: $26M raised across multiple rounds; Series B (April 2023) led by Boathouse Capital; prior investors include Attain Capital and BarronKent

name: Govstream.ai
description: AI copilot for permit technicians, planners, and reviewers that sits on top of existing permitting systems to answer staff questions, validate documents, and pre-check applications against municipal codes. Live in Bellevue WA (30% fewer routine inquiries) and Louisville KY.
funding_detail: $4.9M total; $3.6M Seed (Dec 2025) led by 47th Street Partners; pre-seed from Nellore Capital and Ascend

name: Just Appraised
description: AI workflow software for county assessors and clerks, automating deed processing, ownership transfers, exemptions, and taxpayer communication. Serves 300+ counties in 30 states; YC-backed.
funding_detail: Y Combinator-backed; seed stage; total undisclosed

name: Forerunner
description: AI geospatial platform for government built-environment operations, unifying floodplain compliance, code enforcement, permitting, asset tracking, and grant management with mobile field tools. Used by 190+ communities in 26 states, including CA Department of Water Resources and FL Division of Emergency Management.
funding_detail: $39M total; $26.3M Series B (Feb 2026) led by Wellington Management; prior investors include Gutter Capital

name: Deckard Technologies
description: AI platform (Rentalscape) for short- and long-term rental compliance that scans 15M+ listings daily to find unregistered properties, track permits, collect occupancy taxes, and support enforcement. Used by 400+ jurisdictions; acquired rental data firm AllTheRooms.

name: Aclima
description: Public benefit corporation providing block-by-block air quality and greenhouse gas measurement to environmental agencies via vehicle-mounted sensors. Holds a $27M California Air Resources Board contract; partners include NY State DEC and EPA.
funding_detail: $64M total; $40M Series B (2020); $13M additional round (Sept 2024); investors include Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund, Bosch Ventures, and Kapor Capital

name: Automotus
description: Computer vision platform for automated curb management, monitoring loading zones, automating commercial vehicle payments, enforcing violations, and giving city planners real-time analytics. Deployed in dozens of US markets.
funding_detail: $26M total; $9M equity round (Dec 2025) led by Santa Barbara Venture Partners and Weatherford Capital; $9M seed (2022) led by CityRock Venture Partners

name: DeepWalk
description: iPhone LiDAR software that lets municipal staff scan sidewalks and automatically measures them for ADA compliance, producing maps, reports, and construction documents for ADA transition plans. Serves cities, universities, and engineering consultants; integrates with ArcGIS.

name: Ontra Mobility
description: AI transit planning and dispatch platform that forecasts demand, optimizes fixed routes, and dispatches on-demand service in real time; powered MARTA Reach (Atlanta) and CAT SMART (Savannah). YC S24; selected for the 2026 Transit Tech Lab with MTA NYCT and LIRR.

name: Waypoint Transit
description: AI city planner that automates GIS analysis, data collection, and transportation planning reports for municipalities and transit agencies at about 30% of traditional consultant cost. Live in 10+ jurisdictions including Duluth and MnDOT; YC W25.

name: Waterly
description: Data management and regulatory compliance software for water and wastewater utilities, replacing paper logs with real-time data entry, dosage calculation, compliance reporting, and SCADA integration. Designed by water operators; serves rural communities through large cities.
funding_detail: $4M raised; Series A (Aug 2025) led by Burnt Island Ventures; prior investors include Emerald Technology Ventures and CivStart

name: Mark43
description: Cloud-native public safety platform (dispatch, records management, mobile, and analytics) replacing legacy on-premise systems for police and fire agencies, with CJIS and FedRAMP High compliance. Customers include Department of the Interior law enforcement programs and Dallas police and fire (selected Mar 2026).
funding_detail: ~$141M total raised through Series C (Seedtable); investors include General Catalyst, Spark Capital, Goldman Sachs, and Jeff Bezos

name: CivicEye
description: Unified cloud software for law enforcement, prosecutors, and courts covering records management, digital evidence, and case management. Adopted statewide by the Tennessee District Attorney General Conference; 150+ agencies nationwide.
funding_detail: $12.4M Series A (July 2022) led by Cercano Management; participation from Relevance Ventures

name: Ordinal
description: AI research assistant for local government staff that answers questions with citations from approved internal documents such as municipal codes, ordinances, GIS data, and meeting minutes, without training on external data. Live in cities in Arkansas, Oklahoma, Missouri, and California.
funding_detail: $1M Seed (Aug 2025) led by Plains Ventures; participation from Winrock International and The Venture Center Arkansas Fund

name: GovGuard
description: AI agents for government FOIA and public records work: searching archived records, flagging material for redaction under state exemption codes, and drafting response letters, with clerks keeping full review authority. YC Spring 2026.

name: RapidSOS
description: Public safety platform connecting 600M+ devices and sensors to 22,000+ emergency agencies in real time. Gives 911 dispatchers location, medical, and contextual data through its HARMONY AI system and has supported over one billion emergencies.
funding_detail: $450M+ raised across multiple rounds; $100M round (Nov 2025) led by Apax Digital at $1B valuation; prior investors include Highland Capital Partners, Insight Partners, BlackRock, and NightDragon

name: Swiftly
description: Real-time transit data platform providing operational analytics, on-time performance monitoring, schedule optimization, and passenger information. Works with nearly half of the top 50 US transit agencies, including MBTA, LA Metro, SEPTA, and MDOT MTA.
funding_detail: $200M+ raised across multiple rounds; 2025 strategic investment led by Cove Hill Partners with JMI Equity; prior investors include Renewal Funds, Ford Smart Mobility, and Samsung NEXT

name: The Callimachus Project
description: Nonprofit using AI to capture institutional knowledge from departing federal civil servants. Conducts long-form interviews with former employees, then summarizes, stores, and analyzes the knowledge to build a free, searchable AI chatbot database intended for Hill staff and transition teams working to rebuild civil service capacity.
funding_detail: Private philanthropy via fiscal sponsor has funded founding and early proof of concept; seeking further philanthropic funding to build out AI interview-collection process and chatbot database/interface.

name: Pennsylvania Governor's Science and Technology Fellowship
description: One-year fellowship (launched 2024) placing master's and doctoral STEM graduates in Pennsylvania state agencies on data, technology, and program modernization projects. Inaugural cohort of 11; fellows may be offered permanent state positions. Part of the Shapiro administration's HIRE executive order expanding public service talent pathways.
funding_detail: PA Office of Administration; host agency budgets

name: Renaissance Philanthropy
description: Philanthropic advisor and fund incubator founded in 2024 by former White House science and technology adviser Tom Kalil, building multi-donor initiatives across science, technology, and U.S. state capacity. Funding partner of the Public Benefit Innovation Fund for AI in benefits delivery.

name: Packard Foundation (David and Lucile Packard Foundation)
description: Private foundation whose state capacity grantmaking includes early backing of the Recoding America Fund. Funded the GovAI Coalition's 2026 transition to an independent nonprofit ($150K).

name: Virginia Digital Service
description: New in-house state team (Sept 2026) of engineers, designers, and technical experts working alongside VITA to modernize websites and systems and scrutinize IT contracts. Created after a $52M failed child support system project. Led by founding director Andrea Fletcher, former CMS chief digital strategy officer.

name: CITP Technology Fellows Program (Princeton)
description: Non-residential fellowship (launched 2025) building a network of technologists with government experience who take paid projects for state and local regulators on AI, privacy, data, and digital markets. Inaugural cohort of 6-10 fellows; 5-8 hours a month.
